scientific_question: After the v10.8 full K3 detector-space target passed 5/5 and all diagonal, gain, and nearest controls failed 0/5, does a complete cross-view and cross-frequency linear map have trajectory-level headroom under the unchanged exact A^T, observable alpha, and CGLS K1 downstream path?

data_roles.inner_selection: leave one complete outer-train trajectory out

target.normalization: divide observation and certificate by per-frame observation RMS
target.full_view_target_viability: frozen from independently validated v10.8.2; 5/5 fit trajectories

model_family.definition: z_hat = q X^T (X X^T + lambda I)^-1 Z in normalized detector coordinates
model_family.ridge_scale: median numerically positive eigenvalue of X X^T divided by detector dimension
model_family.zero_ridge: spectral Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse with a deterministic float64 tolerance

arms.selection: minimum equal-trajectory mean normalized-certificate relative-L2 on inner held-out trajectories
lexicographic inner compatibility pass count, severe harm, joint harm, worst observation harm, joint match, target error
best compatibility key on the outer held-out trajectory; non-deployable family-headroom diagnostic

shared_downstream.path: predicted dual -> exact A^T -> observable alpha in [0,2] -> unchanged CGLS K1
shared_downstream.compatibility_gate: unchanged v10.8 field, gradient, and observation envelope

decision.deployable_candidate: either nested selector passes all five outer held-out trajectories
decision.selection_failure: neither nested selector passes all five but the non-deployable outer oracle does
decision.family_failure: the outer oracle itself fails at least one held-out trajectory
decision.nonlinear_authorization: a family failure may justify one minimal nonlinear detector model, but is not itself an algorithm result
